conventions.position: row index of the shuffled `val` split in stream order (files in name order, rows in file order)
conventions.unshuffled_index: row index of the unshuffled `val` split; shuffled row i is unshuffled row perm[i]
conventions.document: row index of the re-split `val` split of danbraunai/pile-uncopyrighted (0 to 999,999)
conventions.tokenization_batch: index of the authors' tokenization batch (0 to 1,119): 160 shards of 6,250 documents, each cut into six batches of 1,000 and one of 250; every row lies inside one batch
conventions.row documents: first_doc to last_doc: the lowest and highest document any token of the row covers by its character span; EOS separators belong to no document
conventions.pile_labels: the distinct meta.pile_set_name of the documents the row's tokens cover, sorted, joined by '|'
conventions.hash: SHA-256 of the row's int32 ids as little-endian bytes (the earlier project's hash_ids)

tokenization_batches.evidence: The dataset card's num_proc = 10 (shards of 100,000, batches at multiples of 1,000) reproduced the first 17,402 unshuffled rows only (documents 0 to 6,008; 2,775,708 rows rebuilt against 2,775,651). In the authors' stream the batch starting at document 6,000 has its first chunk boundary at character 81,626, which among 1 to 1,000 documents only a batch of 250 (documents 6,000 to 6,249) produces; that batch reproduces its 820 rows exactly. num_proc = 160 gives shards of 6,250, hence this batch. The row-hash check below tests it on every row.

eos_check.note: the plan's check, for a batch of n documents: n - 1 EOS tokens. A failing batch's documents are still assigned exactly, by character span; the EOS reading would misassign them
